/-!
# Ramsey-type properties of graph pairs

The Erdős–Hajnal "exceptional pair" trio of predicates:

- `HasFiniteRamseyProperty G₁ G₂` — for every `n ≥ 1` there is a `G₁`-free graph `H` such
  that every `n`-edge-colouring of `H` contains a monochromatic `G₂`.
- `HasCountableRamseyEscape G₁ G₂` — every `G₁`-free graph `H` admits a countable
  edge-colouring with every colour class `G₂`-free.
- `IsErdosHajnalExceptional G₁ G₂` — the conjunction of both.

These were introduced for Erdős Problem 596 but are reusable for Problem 595 and other
Ramsey-type questions; we factor them out per mo271's review.
-/

namespace SimpleGraph

/-- The **finite Ramsey property** for the pair $(G_1, G_2)$: for every $n \geq 1$, there
exists a $G_1$-free graph `H` on some vertex type in `Type` (universe 0) such that every
`n`-edge-colouring of `H` contains a monochromatic copy of `G_2`. -/
def HasFiniteRamseyProperty {U₁ U₂ : Type*}
    (G₁ : SimpleGraph U₁) (G₂ : SimpleGraph U₂) : Prop :=
  ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n →
  ∃ (V : Type) (H : SimpleGraph V),
    G₁.Free H ∧
    ∀ (c : Fin n → SimpleGraph V), H.IsEdgeColouring c →
      ∃ i, G₂ ⊑ c i

/-- The **countable Ramsey escape property** for the pair $(G_1, G_2)$: every $G_1$-free
graph `H` on a `Type`-valued vertex type has a countable edge-colouring in which every
colour class is $G_2$-free. -/
def HasCountableRamseyEscape {U₁ U₂ : Type*}
    (G₁ : SimpleGraph U₁) (G₂ : SimpleGraph U₂) : Prop :=
  ∀ (W : Type) (H : SimpleGraph W),
    G₁.Free H →
    ∃ (d : ℕ → SimpleGraph W),
      H.IsEdgeColouring d ∧ ∀ j, G₂.Free (d j)

/-- A pair $(G_1, G_2)$ is **Erdős–Hajnal exceptional** if it has both the finite Ramsey
property and the countable Ramsey escape property. -/
def IsErdosHajnalExceptional {U₁ U₂ : Type*}
    (G₁ : SimpleGraph U₁) (G₂ : SimpleGraph U₂) : Prop :=
  HasFiniteRamseyProperty G₁ G₂ ∧ HasCountableRamseyEscape G₁ G₂

end SimpleGraph

findings.description: The downstream file FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/596.lean misidentifies its [Er87] reference as “Some of my favourite problems in various branches of combinatorics”, Mat. Lapok (1987). The relevant Erdős source is “Some problems on finite and infinite graphs”, Contemporary Mathematics 65 (1987), 223–228, §5. This is a bibliographic error, not a defect in the theorem or the reusable predicates.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős, “Some problems on finite and infinite graphs”, https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1987-28.pdf, §5, pp. 224–225, discusses precisely the finite-colour versus countably-many-colours question, the C₄/C₆ example, and the K₄/K₃ case. The title and publication details are also recorded in https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the [Er87] bibliography entry in FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/596.lean with the correct title, Contemporary Mathematics 65 (1987), 223–228, and preferably a pointer to §5.

findings.description: In FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/596.lean, this theorem's docstring attributes the C₄-free/C₆ Ramsey construction to [NeRo75], whose bibliography entry is the 1976 paper about forbidden complete subgraphs. The relevant reference for this construction is Nešetřil–Rödl's 1987 “Strong Ramsey theorems for Steiner systems”. The Lean statement itself faithfully states the known result.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős's 1987 paper, §5, p. 225 (https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1987-28.pdf), explicitly identifies the paper giving the C₄-free construction as forthcoming in Transactions of the AMS. Nešetřil–Rödl, “Strong Ramsey theorems for Steiner systems”, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 303 (1987), 183–192, DOI 10.1090/S0002-9947-1987-0896015-8, states in its AMS abstract that graphs without cycles of lengths 3 and 4 have the edge Ramsey property. Applying that result to C₆ and iterating the two-colour assertion gives the stated finite-colour result.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a reference to the 1987 Steiner-systems paper and cite it in C4_C6_finite_ramsey. Retain the forbidden-complete-subgraphs reference for the K₄/K₃ results.

reformulations.difference: An n-edge-colouring is represented by a family of spanning graphs indexed by Fin n whose edge sets partition the host, rather than by a function from the host's edges to Fin n. A monochromatic target is expressed using non-induced containment in one member of that family.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every edge-label function gives its pairwise-disjoint label graphs, whose supremum is the host. Conversely, coverage and disjointness give a unique colour for each host edge, and reconstruct exactly the original family. Mathlib's Copy is an injective adjacency-preserving map, so containment in a label graph is precisely a monochromatic, not necessarily induced, copy. Both the colouring correspondence and the equivalence of the complete finite Ramsey predicates were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean. The source also permits arbitrary host graphs: “finite” concerns the palette, not the vertex set.

reformulations.difference: The definition uses an ℕ-indexed edge partition with every class target-free. The source describes a countable edge-colouring, and the related K₄/K₃ question uses a countable union of triangle-free graphs without requiring disjointness.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The edge-partition/edge-label correspondence works for ℕ as well. An overlapping cover by target-free graphs can be refined by assigning each edge to one covering index. Each resulting colour graph is a subgraph of its original covering graph and remains target-free, since non-induced containment is monotone under adding edges. Conversely, every partition is a cover. Unused colours are allowed, so finite covers are included. The full equivalences with edge labelings and with countable covers, including the K₄/K₃ specialization via Mathlib's cliqueFree_iff_top_free, were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: No mathematical defect was found in Ramsey.lean or in the meanings used by its downstream declarations. All three definitions and every direct use in ErdosProblems/596.lean were checked. The explicitly documented Type-0 host convention is consistent with all actual use sites and imposes no finiteness or countability restriction. The 322-line scratch.lean compiles without errors, warnings, or sorry; it contains the equivalence proofs, symbolic tests for zero/one colours, empty forbidden and target graphs, edgeless targets, and diagonal containment, plus finite computations testing copies, coverage, and disjointness. The two findings are only downstream bibliography corrections. Both relevant problem pages still record the open questions as open. No repository files were edited.
